items.label: Lemma 1
items.title: Polar direction update
items.statementHtml: Let $j\ge0$. Suppose that the polar data have $\rho_k,\zeta_k>0$ and $Z_k\succ0$ for $k=2j,2j+1,2j+2$, and that $0<\delta_k<\pi$ and $(Z_k)_{12}>0$ for $k=2j,2j+1$. The following statements hold for $k=2j,2j+1$: \textup{i)} a unique $\alpha_k>0$ satisfying $s_k=-\alpha_kH_kg_k$ exists if and only if $r_k=\cos\delta_k+h_k\sin\delta_k$; \textup{ii)} if the relations in part~\textup{i)} hold and $p_k^Tq_k>0$ at both stages, then [eq:dfp-update] is equivalent to Z_{k+1}=R(\delta_k)^T \left[ \left(I-\frac{q_kp_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}\right)Z_k \left(I-\frac{p_kq_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}\right) +\frac{q_kq_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k} \right]R(\delta_k).

theorem matrix_step (p : Parameters) (hβ : 0 < p.beta) (hstart : 0 < p.startIndex) (k : ℕ) :
    p.matrix (k + 1) = DFP.Polar.matrixStep (p.matrix k) (p.angleIncrement k)
      (p.zeta k) (p.zeta (k + 1)) := by
  rcases Nat.even_or_odd' k with ⟨j, rfl | rfl⟩
  · rw [matrix_odd, matrix_even, zeta_even, zeta_odd]
    exact oddMatrix_step p hβ hstart j
  · have hindex : 2 * j + 1 + 1 = 2 * (j + 1) := by omega
    rw [hindex, matrix_even, matrix_odd, zeta_odd, zeta_even]
    exact evenMatrix_step p hβ hstart j

items.label: Lemma 2
items.title: Polar endpoint Wolfe ratios
items.statementHtml: Let $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$. Suppose $0<\delta_k<\pi$, $h_k>0$, $\rho_k,\rho_{k+1},\zeta_k,\zeta_{k+1}>0$, and $r_k=\rho_k/\rho_{k+1}=\cos\delta_k+h_k\sin\delta_k$. Then $g_k^Ts_k<0$, and the prescribed values and gradients satisfy the strong Wolfe conditions if and only if(分别编号) \frac{\rho_k^2-\rho_{k+1}^2}{-2g_k^Ts_k} &=\frac{r_k^2-1}{2\zeta_kh_k\sin\delta_k\,r_k}\ge\eta_1,\\ \frac{|g_{k+1}^Ts_k|}{|g_k^Ts_k|} &=\frac{\zeta_{k+1}}{\zeta_k} \frac{|h_k\cos\delta_k-\sin\delta_k|}{h_kr_k}\le\eta_2.

theorem sourceStrongWolfe_of_phaseMargins (p : Parameters) (κ δ H : ℝ)
    (hβ : 0 < p.beta) (hstart : 0 < p.startIndex)
    (hc1 : 0 < p.c1) (hc12 : p.c1 < p.c2) (hc2 : p.c2 < 1)
    (hobjective : Objective.ObjectiveEstimates p κ δ H)
    (hZ : ∀ k, (p.matrix k).PosDef) (hC : ∀ k, 0 < p.matrix k 0 1)
    (hSin : ∀ k, 0 < Real.sin (p.angleIncrement k)) (hW : ∀ k, 0 < p.radiusRatio k)
    (hr : ∀ k, 0 < p.radius k)
    (hlog : Summable (fun j ↦ Real.log (p.radiusRatio (2 * j) * p.radiusRatio (2 * j + 1))))
    (hphase : ∀ j : ℕ, ∀ i : Fin 2,
      p.c1 < RadiusBounds.phaseArmijo p i (p.scale j) (p.inverseIndex j) (p.normalizedEvenState j) ∧
        RadiusBounds.phaseCurvature p i (p.scale j) (p.inverseIndex j)
          (p.normalizedEvenState j) < p.c2)
    (k : ℕ) :
    LineSearch.IsStrongWolfe p.c1 p.c2 (p.objective κ) (p.point k)
      (p.point (k + 1) - p.point k) := by
  apply sourceStrongWolfe_of_rawQuotients p κ δ H hc1 hc12 hc2 hobjective
    hZ hC hSin hW hr hlog
  intro k
  rcases Nat.even_or_odd' k with ⟨j, rfl | rfl⟩
  · have h := hphase j 0
    have hquot := sourceQuotients_eq_phase p hβ hstart j 0
    rw [← hquot.1, ← hquot.2] at h
    simpa only [Fin.val_zero, Nat.add_zero] using And.intro h.1.le h.2.le
  · have h := hphase j 1

items.label: Proposition 3
items.title: Polar DFP realization
items.statement:
\label{prop:polar-realization}
Suppose that
\textup{i)} for every $k\ge0$, the polar data satisfy
$\rho_k,\zeta_k>0$, $Z_k\succ0$, $(Z_k)_{12}>0$,
$0<\delta_k<\pi$, $p_k^Tq_k>0$, and
$r_k=\cos\delta_k+h_k\sin\delta_k$;
\textup{ii)} for fixed $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
\eqref{eq:polar-matrix-map} and \eqref{eq:polar-wolfe-ratios}
hold for every $k\ge0$;
\textup{iii)} a single function $f\in C^1(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfies
$f(x_k)=F_k$ and $\nabla f(x_k)=g_k$ for all $k\ge0$.
Then there are positive step lengths for which classical DFP initialized at
$x_0,H_0$ generates exactly the prescribed points and matrices and
satisfies the strong Wolfe conditions at every step.

theorem existsSourceCertificate (p : Parameters) (κ : ℝ)
    (horbit : DFP.IsOrbit (p.objective κ) p.stepLength p.point p.gradients p.inverseHessian)
    (hpos : ∀ k, (p.inverseHessian k).PosDef)
    (hden : ∀ k,
      WithLp.ofLp (DFP.steps p.stepLength (DFP.directions p.inverseHessian p.gradients) k) ⬝ᵥ
        WithLp.ofLp (DFP.gradientChanges p.gradients k) ≠ 0)
    (hC2 : ContDiff ℝ 2 (p.objective κ))
    (hBounds : HasHessianBounds (1 / 2) (3 / 2) (p.objective κ))
    (hWolfe : ∀ k, LineSearch.IsStrongWolfe p.c1 p.c2 (p.objective κ)
      (p.point k) (p.point (k + 1) - p.point k))
    (hLimit : Tendsto (fun k ↦ ‖p.gradients k‖) atTop (𝓝 1)) :
    ∃ w : DFP.StrongWolfeCounterexample (Fin 2) (1 / 2) (3 / 2) p.c1 p.c2,
      SourceIdentity p κ w ∧ w.gradientLimit = 1 := by
  let it := horbit.toInverseIteration hpos hden
  have hobjective : it.objective = p.objective κ := horbit.toInverseIteration_objective hpos hden
  have hpoint : it.point = p.point := horbit.toInverseIteration_point_eq hpos hden
  have hstepLength : it.stepLength = p.stepLength := horbit.toInverseIteration_stepLength hpos hden
  have hmatrix : it.inverseHessian = p.inverseHessian :=
    horbit.toInverseIteration_inverseHessian_eq hpos hden
  have hgradients : DFP.gradients it.objective it.point = p.gradients := by
    rw [hobjective, hpoint]
    exact horbit.gradients_eq
  have hStep (k : ℕ) : 0 < it.stepLength k := by
    rw [hstepLength]
    exact horbit.stepLengthPos k
  have hStrong (k : ℕ) : LineSearch.IsStrongWolfe p.c1 p.c2 it.objective
      (it.point k) (it.point (k + 1) - it.point k) := by
    simpa only [hobjective, hpoint] using hWolfe k
  have hWeak (k : ℕ) : LineSearch.IsWeakWolfe p.c1 p.c2 it.objective
      (it.point k) (it.point (k + 1) - it.point k) := by
    apply (hStrong k).toWeakWolfe
    simpa only [DFP.gradients_apply] using (it.gradientInnerDisplacementNeg k (hStep k)).le
  have hContDiff : ContDiff ℝ 2 it.objective := by
    rwa [hobjective]
  have hHessian : HasHessianBounds (1 / 2) (3 / 2) it.objective := by
    rwa [hobjective]
  have hTendsto : Tendsto (fun k ↦ ‖DFP.gradients it.objective it.point k‖) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
    simpa only [hgradients] using hLimit
  let weak : DFP.WolfeCounterexample (Fin 2) (1 / 2) (3 / 2) p.c1 p.c2 := {
    iteration := it
    gradientLimit := 1
    objectiveContDiff := hContDiff
    stepLengthPos := hStep
    hessianBounds := hHessian
    weakWolfe := hWeak
    gradientLimitPos := zero_lt_one
    gradientNormTendsto := hTendsto
  }
  let w : DFP.StrongWolfeCounterexample (Fin 2) (1 / 2) (3 / 2) p.c1 p.c2 := {
    toWolfeCounterexample := weak
    strongWolfe := hStrong
  }
  have hw : w.iteration = it := rfl
  have hsource : SourceIdentity p κ w := by
    constructor
    · exact (congrArg DFP.InverseIteration.objective hw).trans hobjective
    · exact congrArg DFP.InverseIteration.point hw |>.trans hpoint
    · exact congrArg DFP.InverseIteration.stepLength hw |>.trans hstepLength
    · exact congrArg DFP.InverseIteration.inverseHessian hw |>.trans hmatrix
    · simpa only [hw] using hgradients
  have hgradientLimit : w.gradientLimit = 1 := rfl
  exact ⟨w, hsource, hgradientLimit⟩

items.label: Lemma 4
items.title: Limiting two-cycle
items.statementHtml: Fix $X\succ0$ with $\xi>0$, and for each $\tau>0$ set $Z_k=S_\tau^{-1}XS_\tau^{-1}$. If $\delta_k/\tau\to\bar\delta>0$ and $\zeta_k,\zeta_{k+1}\to1$ as $\tau\downarrow0$, then the update [eq:polar-matrix-map] is well defined for all sufficiently small $\tau>0$, and $S_\tau Z_{k+1}S_\tau$ tends to the symmetric matrix X_+=\gamma_+&\xi_+\\\xi_+&\eta_+ =\gamma&\gamma(\bar h-\bar\delta)\\\gamma(\bar h-\bar\delta)&1+\gamma(\bar h-\bar\delta)^2.

items.label: Lemma 5
items.title: Admissible parameter choice
items.statement:
\label{lem:polar-parameter-choice}
For every $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, one can choose positive angular
coefficients and a base point $\nu_*$ in the positivity interval of
\eqref{eq:polar-family} so that, with $\gamma_*=\gamma(\nu_*)$,
the following hold: \textup{i)} at both the even and odd stages,
the limiting Armijo and strong-curvature ratios are respectively
above $\eta_1$ and below $\eta_2$;
\textup{ii)} at the even state corresponding to $\nu_*$, with
$\gamma=\gamma_*$ fixed, the derivative of the complete limiting
cycle in $(\xi,\eta)$ has spectral radius less than one;
\textup{iii)} $\gamma'(\nu_*)>0$, so $\gamma(\nu)$ has an analytic
local inverse $\nu(\gamma)$ near $\gamma_*$.

theorem strictWolfeBaseExists {c1 c2 : ℝ} (hc1 : 0 < c1)
    (hc12 : c1 < c2) (hc2 : c2 < 1) :
    ∃ ell z : ℝ, StrictWolfeBase c1 c2 ell z := by
  by_cases hthird : (1 : ℝ) / 3 < c2
  · exact strictWolfeBaseAboveThird hc12 hc2 hthird
  · exact strictWolfeBaseBelowThird (lt_trans hc1 hc12) hc12 (le_of_not_gt hthird)

items.label: Lemma 6
items.title: Two-cycle estimates
items.statement:
\label{lem:polar-cycle-estimates}
Fix a positive analytic function $\phi$ on a neighborhood of the
chosen $\gamma$ interval, and let $\Phi$ be the complete cycle defined
above. Then $\Phi$ extends analytically to $\tau^2=v=0$.
After shrinking the chosen $\gamma$ interval about $\gamma_*$ if
necessary, there are a fixed norm
$|\cdot|_*$, $0<q<1$, and $\kappa_0>0$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:polar-fast-bound}
\begin{aligned}
 |u_+|_*&\le q|u|_*+\kappa_0(v+\tau^2)+\kappa_0|u|_*^2,\\
 \gamma_+&=\gamma+v\psi_\phi(\gamma)
          +O(v|u|_*+v^2+\tau^2),
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}\label{eq:polar-slow-drift}
 \psi_\phi(\gamma)
 =2\gamma\nu(\gamma)
 \left(\bar\delta_{\mathrm E}^{-1}+\bar\delta_{\mathrm O}^{-1}\right)
 \phi(\gamma)-\frac{2\gamma}{1+\beta}.
\end{equation}
The bounds are uniform for sufficiently small $\tau^2,v\ge0$ and states
in a fixed neighborhood of the even reference curve, with constants
depending on $\phi$.

items.label: Lemma 7
items.title: Infinite polar continuation
items.statement:
\label{lem:polar-continuation}
For every sufficiently large $j_0$, the recurrence
\eqref{eq:polar-matrix-map}, initialized by
\eqref{eq:polar-initial-matrix}, with the angles in
\eqref{eq:polar-angles} and the gradient factors in
\eqref{eq:polar-feedback}, defines an infinite matrix sequence. For all $j\ge0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:polar-tube-estimates}
 \gamma_j=\gamma_*+O(\tau_j^{1-\beta}),\qquad
 X_j-X_{\mathrm E}(\gamma_j)=O(\tau_j^{1+\beta}).
\end{equation}
The odd normalized matrices satisfy
$S_{\tau_j}Z_{2j+1}S_{\tau_j}=X_{\mathrm O}(\gamma_j)+O(\tau_j^{1+\beta})$.
Every matrix $Z_k$ is positive definite, and
$(Z_k)_{12}>0$, $r_k>0$, and $p_k^Tq_k>0$.
The constants are independent of $j_0$ once $j_0$ exceeds a fixed threshold.

theorem existsContinuationEstimates (p : Parameters) (hβ : 0 < p.beta) (hβone : p.beta < 1) :
    ∃ N > 0, ∃ M > 0, ∃ K > 0, ∃ J : ℕ, 0 < J ∧ ∀ j0 : ℕ, J ≤ j0 →
      TrajectoryBounds p j0 N M ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, RawFeasible (p.withStartIndex j0) k) ∧
        ∀ j : ℕ,
          ‖(p.withStartIndex j0).normalizedOddState j - p.oddReference (stateAt p j0 j).1‖ ≤
            K / ((j0 + j : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
  obtain ⟨CO, hCO, rO, hrO, ρO, hρO, εO, hεO, hodd⟩ := exists_localOdd_bound p hβ
  obtain ⟨N, hN, M, hM, J0, hJ0, hcontinuation⟩ := existsContinuation p hβ hβone
  obtain ⟨J1, hinside⟩ := exists_barrier_threshold hβ hβone N M rO ρO hrO hρO
  obtain ⟨J2, hsmall⟩ := exists_smallParameter_threshold hβ hεO
  let K := CO * (N + 2)
  have hK : 0 < K := by
    dsimp [K]
    positivity
  refine ⟨N, hN, M, hM, K, hK, max J0 (max J1 J2), hJ0.trans_le (le_max_left _ _), ?_⟩
  intro j0 hj0
  have hj00 : J0 ≤ j0 := (le_max_left _ _).trans hj0
  have hj01 : J1 ≤ j0 := (le_max_left _ _).trans ((le_max_right _ _).trans hj0)
  have hj02 : J2 ≤ j0 := (le_max_right _ _).trans ((le_max_right _ _).trans hj0)
  have hstart : 0 < j0 := hJ0.trans_le hj00
  have hbase := hcontinuation j0 hj00
  refine ⟨hbase.1, hbase.2, ?_⟩
  intro j
  have hi := hinside j0 hj01 j

items.label: Lemma 8
items.title: Polar geometry and separation
items.statementHtml: For sufficiently large $j_0$, the points in [eq:polar-radii] have accumulation set $\Gamma=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x\|=1\}$ and satisfy \|x_m-x_k\|\ge \kappa_-\max\{\tau_{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}, \tau_{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\} \qquad(m\ne k), where $\kappa_->0$ is independent of $j_0$. Moreover, $\|s_k\|\asymp\tau_{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}$, $\|g_k-x_k\|=O(\tau_{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}^{1+\beta})$, and the endpoint data $F_k,g_k$ satisfy the strong Wolfe inequalities at every step. The comparison constants are independent of $j_0$.

theorem existsSourceGeometry (p : Parameters) (hβ : 0 < p.beta) (hβone : p.beta < 1) :
    ∃ N > 0, ∃ M > 0, ∃ B > 0, ∃ K > 0, ∃ c > 0, ∃ U > 0,
      ∃ a > 0, ∃ b > 0, ∃ s > 0, ∃ V > 0, ∃ J : ℕ, 0 < J ∧
        ∀ j0 : ℕ, J ≤ j0 → SourceGeometricData p j0 N M B K c U a b s V := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN, M, hM, B, hB, K, hK, c, hc, U, hU, JR, hJR, hRadial⟩ :=
    RadiusProducts.existsSourceRadialData p hβ hβone
  obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, JA, hJA, hAngles⟩ := AngularBounds.existsAngleBoundsWithSin p hβ
  let η := min 1 (Real.pi / b)
  have hη : 0 < η := lt_min zero_lt_one (div_pos Real.pi_pos hb)
  have hηone : η ≤ 1 := min_le_left _ _
  have hspan : b * η ≤ Real.pi := by
    have h := (le_div_iff₀ hb).mp (min_le_right 1 (Real.pi / b))
    simpa only [mul_comm] using h
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hSep⟩ := Geometry.exists_uniform_point_separation
    hβ hη hηone ha hb.le hc hspan
  have hsmall := (scale_tendsto_zero hβ 0).eventually (Iio_mem_nhds (half_pos hη))
  obtain ⟨JS, hJS⟩ := eventually_atTop.mp hsmall
  let V := U + B * b
  have hV : 0 < V := add_pos hU (mul_pos hB hb)
  refine ⟨N, hN, M, hM, B, hB, K, hK, c, hc, U, hU, a, ha, b, hb,
    s, hs, V, hV, max JR (max JA JS), hJR.trans_le (le_max_left _ _), ?_⟩
  intro j0 hj0
  have hjR : JR ≤ j0 := (le_max_left _ _).trans hj0
  have hjA : JA ≤ j0 := (le_max_left _ _).trans ((le_max_right _ _).trans hj0)

items.label: Lemma 9
items.title: Explicit polar interpolation
items.statementHtml: Let $x_k,g_k,F_k$ be the data in Lemma~[lem:polar-geometry], with $j_0$ sufficiently large. Then there is a function $f\in C^2(\mathbb R^2)$ whose Hessian is globally $ eta$-H\"older continuous and which agrees with $\|x\|^2/2$ on the closed unit disk. At every prescribed point, f(x_k)=F_k= rac{1}{2} ho_k^2,\qquad abla f(x_k)=g_k,\qquad abla^2f(x_k)=I. Writing $\Psi=f-\|x\|^2/2$, there is a constant $\kappa$ independent of the final choice of $j_0$ such that \sup_{x\in\mathbb R^2}\| abla^2\Psi(x)\|\le \kappa au_0^ eta.

theorem existsSourceObjectiveData (p : Parameters) (hβ : 0 < p.beta)
    (hβone : p.beta < 1) (ε : ℝ) (hεpos : 0 < ε) (hε : ε < 1) :
    ∃ N > 0, ∃ M > 0, ∃ κ > 0, ∃ H ≥ 0, ∃ s > 0, ∃ Ustep > 0, ∃ Cobj ≥ 0,
      ∃ J : ℕ, 0 < J ∧ ∀ j0 : ℕ, J ≤ j0 →
        SourceObjectiveData p j0 N M κ ε H ∧
          SourceGeometricData (p.withStartIndex j0) κ s Ustep Cobj := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN, M, hM, B, hB, K, hK, c, hc, U, hU,
    a, ha, b, hb, s, hs, V, hV, J0, hJ0, hgeometry⟩ :=
      ActualGeometry.existsSourceGeometry p hβ hβone
  have hcluster (j0 : ℕ) (hj0 : J0 ≤ j0) :
      {x | MapClusterPt x atTop (p.withStartIndex j0).point} = Metric.sphere 0 1 := by

items.label: Theorem 10
items.title: Strong-Wolfe counterexample
items.statement:
\label{thm:main}
For every integer $n\ge2$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
$\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, and $\beta\in(0,1)$, there exist
$f\in C^2(\R^n)$, $x_0\in\R^n$, a positive definite matrix
$H_0\in\R^{n\times n}$, and a sequence of positive step lengths
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]
$(1-\varepsilon)I\preceq\nabla^2f(x)\preceq(1+\varepsilon)I$
for all $x\in\R^n$, and the origin is the unique minimizer.
\item[(ii)]
The Hessian is globally $\beta$-H\"older continuous and has no
H\"older bound of any exponent $\beta'\in(\beta,1]$ on the
initial level set $\{x:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}$.
\item[(iii)]
The resulting infinite classical DFP sequence satisfies the
standard strong Wolfe conditions with parameters $(\eta_1,\eta_2)$
at every iteration, but $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to1$.
Its accumulation set is the unit circle centered at the origin
in a two-dimensional subspace of $\R^n$.
\end{enumerate}

Its accumulation set is the unit circle centered at the origin in a two-dimensional subspace of $\R^n$.

items.label: Corollary 11
items.title: Identity initialization
items.statement:
\label{cor:identity-initialization}
For every integer $n\ge2$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
and $\beta\in(0,1)$, a strongly convex objective function
$\widetilde f\in C^2(\R^n)$ with globally $\beta$-H\"older continuous
Hessian admits an infinite classical DFP sequence initialized with
$\widetilde H_0=I$, satisfying the standard strong Wolfe conditions
with parameters $(\eta_1,\eta_2)$ and
$\liminf_k\|\nabla\widetilde f(\widetilde x_k)\|>0$.
The origin is its unique minimizer, $\widetilde f(0)=0$, and its Hessian
has positive global lower and upper bounds that may depend on the
example. The accumulation set is an ellipse centered at the origin
in a two-dimensional subspace.

items.label: Lemma 12
items.title: Planar secant degeneration
items.statement:
\label{lem:planar-degeneration}
Let $f\in C^2(\R^2)$ be $m$-strongly convex, where $m>0$.
Consider an infinite sequence of nonstationary iterates with
$g_k=\nabla f(x_k)$, $s_k=-\alpha_kH_kg_k$,
$x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k$, and $y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k$, where $H_k\succ0$,
$\alpha_k>0$, and every step satisfies \eqref{eq:armijo} and
\eqref{eq:weak-curvature} for fixed $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$.
Suppose $H_ky_{k-1}=s_{k-1}$ for $k\ge1$. Put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:planar-scalar-definition}
\kappa_k=\frac{s_k^Ty_k}{\|s_k\|^2}\quad(k\ge0),\qquad
\lambda_k=\kappa_{k-1}\det H_k\quad(k\ge1).
\end{equation}
If $x_k$ does not converge to the unique minimizer $x_*$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:planar-degeneration}
0<\lambda_k\le C\|s_{k-1}\|\|s_k\|\longrightarrow0
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $k$, with $C$ independent of $k$.
Moreover, $\{H_k\}$ is bounded and $\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\to0$.

items.label: Theorem 13
items.title: Planar convergence
items.statement:
\label{thm:planar-convergence}
Let $f\in C^2(\R^2)$ satisfy $\nabla^2f(x)\succeq m I$ for all
$x\in\R^2$ and some $m>0$. Let $x_0\in\R^2$ and $H_0\succ0$
be arbitrary, and fix $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$. Suppose $\nabla^2f$ is locally
Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of the initial level set
$\mathcal L_0=\{x\in\R^2:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}$.
Then classical DFP with update \eqref{eq:dfp-update} and positive step
lengths satisfying \eqref{eq:armijo} and \eqref{eq:weak-curvature}
either reaches the unique minimizer $x_*$ in finitely many iterations or
generates an infinite sequence satisfying
$x_k\longrightarrow x_*$ and $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\longrightarrow0$.

Suppose $ abla^2f$ is locally Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of the initial level set $\mathcal L_0=\{x\in\R^2:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}$. Then classical DFP with update [eq:dfp-update] and positive step lengths satisfying [eq:armijo] and [eq:weak-curvature] either reaches the unique minimizer $x_*$ in finitely many iterations or generates an infinite sequence satisfying $x_k\longrightarrow x_*$ and $\| abla f(x_k)\|\longrightarrow0$.

theorem planarConvergenceCases
    {f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ} {α : ℕ → ℝ}
    {x g : ℕ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)} {H : ℕ → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ}
    (orbit : DFP.IsOrbit f α x g H) {μ c₁ c₂ : ℝ}
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) (hμ : 0 < μ)
    (hHessian : ∀ z v, μ * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ (gradient f) z v) v)
    (hH₀ : (H 0).PosDef)
    (hWolfe : ∀ k, LineSearch.IsWeakWolfe c₁ c₂ f (x k) (x (k + 1) - x k))
    (hNeighborhood : ∃ U : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), IsOpen U ∧
      {z | f z ≤ f (x 0)} ⊆ U ∧ LocallyLipschitzOn U (fderiv ℝ (gradient f))) :
    ∃ xstar, (∀ z, f xstar ≤ f z) ∧ (∀ y, (∀ z, f y ≤ f z) → y = xstar) ∧
      ((∃ K : ℕ, gradient f (x K) = 0 ∧ x K = xstar ∧ ∀ k, K ≤ k → x k = xstar) ∨
        ((∀ k, gradient f (x k) ≠ 0) ∧ Tendsto x atTop (𝓝 xstar) ∧
          Tendsto (fun k ↦ ‖gradient f (x k)‖) atTop (𝓝 0))) := by
  exact DFPWolfe.V21.planarConvergenceCases orbit hf hμ hHessian hH₀ hWolfe hNeighborhood

end DFPWolfe.Latest
